HIGH YIELD — Memory line

### 1 Definition
- Osteochondroma (osteocartilaginous exostosis) → **benign latent** · cartilage origin → a cartilage-capped bony projection on the bone surface, with its **own growth plate**; growth stops at maturity · a malformation (Campbell) or a neoplasm from EXT (exostosin) loss (OKU Tumors 4)

### 2 Origin
- Aberrant cartilage of the **perichondrial ring** (Handbook: "herniated physis beneath periosteum") → stalk by endochondral ossification; the **cap is the neoplastic part** · sporadic lesions → **EXT1** (8q24) loss, homozygous in the cap in 90% (OKU Tumors 4)

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **2nd–3rd decades** · **Sex** → slight **male** predominance · **Relative incidence** → **commonest benign bone lesion**, ≈30% of benign lesions (OKU Tumors 4) · single in ≈90%; multiple → MHE (multiple hereditary exostoses) below

PITFALL — how common?
- Prof Abosena → 45% of benign, 12% of all · Handbook → commonest "when hamartomas are included" · Greenspan → 20–50% of benign
- Say → "**the commonest benign bone tumour**, a third of benign lesions"

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **Metaphyseal**, **Transverse** → **surface**; the stalk points **away from the physis** · never in bone not preformed in cartilage (Campbell)
- **Knee** (distal femur, proximal tibia, proximal fibula) > proximal humerus · **Special sites** → less often scapula (a large one → **pseudo-winging**), pelvis, ribs, spine

### 1 Definition
- Enchondroma (chondroma) → **benign latent** · cartilage origin → **mature hyaline cartilage** inside the medulla · hand lesions look cellular yet stay benign → **benign active** · the surface form → **periosteal (juxtacortical) chondroma** ("ecchondroma", Handbook)

### 2 Origin
- A rest of growth-plate cartilage trapped in the metaphysis, carried to the shaft with growth · somatic **IDH1 / IDH2** mutations (D-2-hydroxyglutarate blocks bone differentiation) → not inherited · multiple → **Ollier, Maffucci** below (OKU Tumors 4)

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **Any age**, diagnosed at 30–50 · **Sex** → **exception: no sex predilection** · **Relative incidence** → **second commonest benign cartilage tumour**, 13% of benign (OKU Tumors 4) · **commonest tumour of the hand** bones

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **Metaphyseal**, **Transverse** → **central** in long bones; diaphyseal + metaphyseal in the hand · **special** → rib, sternum, carpals · never → a solitary spinal lesion is very rare
- **Hands and feet ≈50%** (proximal and middle phalanges, metacarpals) > proximal humerus > distal femur (OKU Tumors 4) · groups → **central · expansile** in the hand → 1 Differential

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Asymptomatic**, found on a knee or shoulder film | None | Hand → **pathological fracture**, the commonest first sign |
| Hand or foot → swelling ± pain | — | Proximal humerus → look for another cause of pain, e.g. rotator cuff |

### 1 Definition
- Chondroblastoma (Codman tumour) → usually stage 2 (**benign active**), rarely stage 3 (**benign aggressive**) · cartilage origin (Campbell) → a rare benign cartilage tumour of the **epiphysis** of young patients

### 2 Origin
- Chondroblasts = cartilage cells of limited differentiation, no type II collagen · gene **H3F3B K36M** in 90% (GCT carries H3F3A G34W) (OKU Tumors 4) · hosts a **secondary ABC** in ≈20% → fluid–fluid levels (Campbell)

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **10–25 years**, before maturity · **Sex** → **male 2 : 1** · **Relative incidence** → **≈1%** of primary bone tumours (Campbell) · hindfoot and flat bones → older patients

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **Epiphyseal** or apophyseal, **Transverse** → **eccentric**; may cross the open physis · never purely metaphyseal or diaphyseal (Greenspan)
- **Distal femur, proximal tibia, proximal humerus** (Campbell) · **special** → greater trochanter, greater tuberosity, patella · hands and feet 10%, talus and calcaneus first there (Greenspan) · groups → **epiphyseal · giant-cell lesions** → 1 Differential

- **Matrix?** → none on the film
- **Histology?** → lobules, stellate cells in myxoid stroma, giant cells at the edge
- **Differential?** → NOF, ABC, GCT, chondrosarcoma
